To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human biartricular hamstrings are stretched across a wide range of running speeds, with differences in the amount of stretch and the speed of stretch occurring in different hamstrings muscles.

with faster running, the biarticular hamstring MTU stretch and stretch velocity patterns remained similar but maxima and mimima increased, activation duration was similar but activation magnitude increased, and the amount of MTUs stretch that occurred during swing after activation had begun was less for the long head of the biarticular biceps femoris compared to the semimembranosus and semitendinosu.

the biarticular hamstring muscle–tendon units (MTUs) were stretched more and shortened faster with faster running speeds, and the activation patterns of these muscles changed in a manner that allowed them to function in a manner appropriate to their role in running.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuro-mechanical function of the human bi-articular hamstrings across the speed spectrum of running.
the neuro-mechanical function of the human bi-articular hamstrings in running, and how this function changes with faster running.
the role of the hamstrings in the human lower limb during running and the factors that influence their activation and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hamstrings are active throughout running, but the timing of activation and the amount of MTUs stretch is speed-dependent.
the human biartcular hamstrings are activated in a similar manner across the range of running speeds studied here, and that there are differences in their neuro-mechanical characteristics.
the biarticular hamstring muscles (SM, ST and BHL) are activated in terminal stance to control the hip flexion angle and the knee extension angle during terminal swing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human biartical hamstrings have a complex role in running.
the biarticular hamstring muscles are stretched and activated in a similar manner across a range of speeds, with some notable differences between the three muscles.
the hamstrings are active throughout the gait cycle, and that they are active at a time when they can contribute to the generation of forward propulsion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hamstrings are activated across a range of speeds, but the amount of activation increases with running speed.
the hamstrings are not simply activated to decelerate the leg at foot-strike.
the biarticular ham-strings are active across a wide range of running speeds to control MTU length and velocity.
